_note: Written for each journey by hand, from the facts in the rate sheet (route, nights, hotels, accommodation tier) and the district guide. `summary` is the one-or-two-sentence line on the card and in the journey header; `story` is the full write-up behind the "read the full description" dialog and on the journey page, one paragraph per blank line. `cover` names a file in public/images/sl that the importer uploads to the media library the first time, so it stays swappable in the admin console. Nothing here is copied from a source document.

Pearl Trail.summary: The island in five days: Sigiriya at first light, the painted caves at Dambulla, the ruined capital of Polonnaruwa, and a night in Kandy before you fly home.
Pearl Trail.story:
Five days is enough for the Sri Lanka most people picture: a rock fortress above the jungle, caves full of painted Buddhas, a ruined city you can cover by bicycle, and the temple in Kandy where the drums start at dusk. We keep it to four driving stages and three hotel moves, so the days stay full without turning into a coach tour.

It opens in Colombo with a city afternoon - Gangaramaya temple, the Pettah market, the sea wall at Galle Face - then drives north to Sigiriya. The climb is the set piece: water gardens, the mirror wall, the frescoes in their sheltered pocket, and the lion's paw at the foot of the last staircase. That evening we send you up Pidurangala, the hill opposite, where the light goes gold on the rock you climbed that morning. Day three brings the five painted caves at Dambulla and Polonnaruwa, where the Gal Vihara's four Buddhas are carved straight into a granite face. Kandy closes the loop: the Temple of the Tooth for the evening puja, and a Kandyan drumming and dance show if you want the theatrical version.

Hotels are four-star and well placed - a city hotel in Colombo, a resort under the rock, a lake lodge at Polonnaruwa and a colonial-era favourite in Kandy. The Cultural Triangle sits in the dry zone and works for most of the year. With two or three days to spare, the natural additions are the tea country above Kandy or a beach at the end, and both are easy to bolt on.

Emerald Escape.summary: Sigiriya and the elephant gathering at Minneriya, then the tea road up to Nuwara Eliya and a dawn at World's End.
Emerald Escape.story:
This is the short trip we recommend most often: the two things people come to Sri Lanka for - the ancient rock and the hill country - with a jeep safari in between and very little wasted driving. Six days, four hotels, one long transfer at the start and a straight run back to the airport at the end.

From Colombo you head north to Sigiriya, climbing the fortress early and spending the afternoon in a jeep at Minneriya, where herds gather on the drying tank bed from roughly July to October; when the water moves, Kaudulla takes over. Dambulla's caves and a spice garden at Matale fill the next morning before Kandy: the lake, the temple, and the drumming at the evening puja. Then the road starts to climb. Peradeniya's botanical gardens, a train ride into the tea estates, a factory walk where you follow the leaf from the weighing scale at the top of the building down to the sorting room at the bottom, and cool nights in Nuwara Eliya. The last full day belongs to Horton Plains: World's End before the mist arrives, Baker's Falls on the way back, and strawberries from a roadside farm on the road home.

Expect two climates in one week - thirty degrees in the dry zone and nearer twelve at night in the hills, so pack a jacket. The hotels are comfortable four-star: a city hotel, an eco-resort under the rock, a riverside hotel in Kandy and a hill hotel in Nuwara Eliya. If you can stretch to eight days, add a beach.

Sapphire Serenity.summary: Three holidays in one week: the rock fortress and the temple of the tooth, the tea country by train, then whales and warm sand at Mirissa.
Sapphire Serenity.story:
A week, three settings. Two nights in the Cultural Triangle, two in the hills, two on the south coast - which is the closest thing to a complete first trip you can do in seven days without spending it in a vehicle.

Sigiriya and Pidurangala take the first full day: the climb in the morning, the view back onto it at sunset. Dambulla's caves on the way to Kandy, where the Temple of the Tooth holds its evening puja and the Kandyan dancers perform an hour later. Then the train - the stretch from Kandy up through the tea estates is the reason people talk about Sri Lankan railways - with a factory visit and a night in Nuwara Eliya. Horton Plains at first light, the Nine Arch Bridge and the short, steep walk up Little Adam's Peak fill the second hill day. From Ella you drop south to Mirissa for two nights: whale watching in the morning from November to April, Parrot Rock for a swim, coconut palms and a seafood dinner at the water's edge. Galle Fort, all ramparts and Dutch-era streets, is on the way back to the airport.

The hotels are a grade above the standard loop - a resort under Sigiriya, a colonial hotel in Kandy, a glass-fronted lodge in Ella and a boutique hillside hotel above Mirissa. Two notes: train seats sell out in the high season, and the whales are seasonal, so tell us your dates and we will plan the week around them.

Golden Circuit.summary: The classic loop with a full day in Yala built in: leopards and sloth bears at dawn, then the south coast for whales and sand.
Golden Circuit.story:
Most one-week itineraries treat Yala as a drive-through: in at dawn, out by lunch, back on the road. This one gives it a proper day, which is why the wildlife is the part people remember. Eight days, six hotels, and a route that keeps moving in one direction instead of doubling back.

Sigiriya and the Minneriya elephant gathering set the tone, with the Dambulla caves and a Matale spice garden on the way to Kandy. Then the train to Ella through the tea estates, the Nine Arch Bridge, and a day on foot: Ella Rock in the morning, Little Adam's Peak for the light at the end of the afternoon, Ravana Falls on the way past. Yala gets a full day - the gate opens at half past five and the convoys follow shortly after, so we go in with the first vehicles, come back for lunch and a swim, and return for the last two hours when the light softens and the animals move.

Two nights at Mirissa follow: whales offshore in season, a surf lesson at Weligama if you want one, and nothing at all if you do not. Galle's Dutch fort closes the trip before the airport run. Hotels are five-star, including a resort on the Yala boundary where the monkeys are a genuine hazard at breakfast.

Royal Odyssey.summary: Nine days from the sacred city of Anuradhapura to the sand at Unawatuna, with the rock, the tea country and a night beside Yala in between.
Royal Odyssey.story:
Nine days is where an itinerary stops feeling like a checklist. This one opens in the old north-central plain rather than at the beach, works down through the rock fortress and the hill country, and finishes with two nights on the south coast.

A slow first day at Negombo - the lagoon, the fishing harbour, seafood by the water - then Anuradhapura, the island's first great capital: the Sri Maha Bodhi grown from a cutting of the tree the Buddha sat under, the Ruwanwelisaya stupa, and a landscape of monasteries and tanks that takes a full day to absorb. Sigiriya and Dambulla follow, with a Minneriya safari in the late afternoon. Kandy gives you the temple, the lake and the dancers. The train to Nuwara Eliya climbs through the estates, and after a tea factory and a night in the hills the road runs down to Ella: Nine Arch Bridge, Ella Rock at sunrise, and Horton Plains behind you. Yala gets a dusk drive and a full day, and then the coast - Unawatuna for swimming and snorkelling, Galle Fort for the last evening.

With four-night stops averaged at two, this is a comfortable trip rather than a rushed one. The hotels are the best of their kind on each stop: a planter's bungalow near Anuradhapura, a resort under Sigiriya, the old grande dame in Nuwara Eliya, a tented camp beside Yala and a hillside hotel above Unawatuna.

Platinum Paradise.summary: The grand tour with the hotels to match: a planter's bungalow, a tea factory you sleep in, a tented camp beside Yala and a beach house at the end.
Platinum Paradise.story:
Ten days of the island at its most comfortable, planned so that the places you sleep are part of the trip rather than a place to park the bags. A restored planter's bungalow on a working estate near Anuradhapura. Two nights in a tea factory above Nuwara Eliya, still with its own chimney and sorting rooms. A tented camp on the edge of Yala, where dinner is served under lanterns and the night is genuinely loud. And a beach house at the end with nothing to do but swim.

Between them: the Negombo lagoon by boat, the sacred city of Anuradhapura, Sigiriya's frescoes and mirror wall, the Dambulla caves, Kandy's temple and botanical gardens, the Ambuluwawa tower for the panorama, and the train into the hills. Horton Plains at first light, Hakgala's gardens and the Moon Plains in the afternoon. Ella and the Nine Arch Bridge, then Udawalawe for elephants in numbers and Yala for a leopard drive at dusk. The last day runs along the coast - whales off Mirissa, the Dutch fort at Galle - before the airport.

What the extra spend actually buys: a private guide and vehicle throughout, private boat charters, a hot-air balloon over the Cultural Triangle if the weather agrees, and a candlelit dinner in the bush. Ultra-luxury hotels, ten days, and no more than two consecutive long drives.

Emerald Isle Explorer.summary: Ten days among the old capitals - Anuradhapura's stupas, Polonnaruwa by bicycle, Dambulla's painted caves - then south to Galle and Mirissa.
Emerald Isle Explorer.story:
Some people come for the beaches; this trip is for the other sort. Ten days given to the island's archaeology and its living religious sites, with two nights in Anuradhapura and two in Kandy so that neither is a drive-past, and the coast saved for the end as a reward.

Negombo's fish market and Dutch canal are a gentle first morning, then three and a half hours north to Anuradhapura: the Sacred Bodhi Tree, the Ruwanwelisaya and Jetavanaramaya stupas, the Abhayagiri monastery, and a full second day that takes in Mihintale at dawn, Isurumuniya, the twin ponds and the museum. Polonnaruwa is next - the Gal Vihara's rock-cut Buddhas, the Vatadage, the royal palace, and the Parakrama Samudra reservoir that still irrigates the district - best covered by bicycle. Sigiriya and Dambulla follow: the climb, the frescoes, and five caves holding something like a hundred and fifty statues under painted ceilings. Kandy adds the temple, Peradeniya's gardens, a spice and herb garden and the Kandyan drumming. Then the tea road to Nuwara Eliya, a factory visit and a tasting. The last two days go south: Galle Fort, walked properly with the lighthouse, the Dutch Reformed Church and the ramparts at sunset, then Mirissa for whales and a swim off Parrot Rock.

Two of the drives run three to four hours, and the hotels are superior grade, including a night inside the fort at Galle. The southern coast is at its best from November to April; the Cultural Triangle is workable all year.

Jungle & Coast Odyssey.summary: Twelve days for people who came for the animals: quiet Wilpattu, elephants at Udawalawe, Yala's leopards and turtles hatching at Rekawa.
Jungle & Coast Odyssey.story:
Three national parks, a turtle beach and enough time in each to stop counting sightings. Wilpattu comes first because almost nobody goes there: it is the largest park in the country, its shallow sand-rimmed lakes - villus - are beautiful in a quiet way, and a leopard sighting is yours alone rather than forty vehicles deep.

Two full days of morning and evening drives there, then Anuradhapura's sacred city, Sigiriya and the elephant gathering at Minneriya or Kaudulla, Dambulla's caves and Kandy's temple. The mountain road to Ella takes you into the tea country, and after the Nine Arch Bridge and Little Adam's Peak the route drops to Udawalawe, where elephants are close to certain and the transit home next door rehabilitates orphaned calves. Two nights at Tangalle follow - a turtle watch at Rekawa after dark, the blow hole, snorkelling in the bay - and then Yala for a full day of morning and afternoon drives: leopards, elephants, sloth bears, crocodiles and painted storks. Galle Fort and the airport close the loop.

A safari day is not a zoo visit: the gates open at half past five, the mornings are cold, the afternoons are hot, and the best sightings happen while the engine is off and everyone is quiet. We do not drive off the track, bait animals or crowd them. Tented camps in Wilpattu and Yala, and a beach villa on the south coast.

Tea Trail & Southern Loop.summary: Thirteen days weighted towards the hills: tea factories and the Kandy-Ella line, Horton Plains at first light, then whales and the Galle fort.
Tea Trail & Southern Loop.story:
The longest look at the hill country we offer. Two nights each in Kandy, Nuwara Eliya, Ella and Mirissa, which is enough to walk an estate, learn how the leaf is fired, and still have an afternoon with nothing in it. The cultural triangle opens the trip and the south coast closes it, but the middle belongs to the hills.

Sigiriya and Pidurangala, then a Minneriya safari in season, Dambulla's golden cave temple, and on to Kandy for the temple, the lake, the gem museum and the fire-walking show. The Pedro Tea Estate gives you the full process and a tasting, and Horton Plains the following morning gives you World's End and Baker's Falls before the cloud comes in. The train from Nuwara Eliya down to Ella runs through the Demodara loop and past the Nine Arch Bridge, which is the photograph everyone brings home. A day on Ella Rock, a rice-and-curry cooking class, then south to Mirissa: whales offshore from November to April, a surf lesson at Weligama or the turtle hatchery if you would rather stay dry, and Coconut Tree Hill at sunset. Galle Fort gets a proper day, and the Handunugoda tea estate - the one that makes virgin white tea - is on the way to the airport.

We book the observation carriage where it exists. Hill-country nights are cold, the coast is warm, and thirteen days means you can be lazy in both. Luxury hotels throughout, including a beachfront villa at Mirissa and a night inside the fort.

Grand Circle Tour.summary: The full loop with the east coast in it: the ancient cities, Trincomalee's reef and hot springs, the tea country, then Yala and Galle.
Grand Circle Tour.story:
The island has two monsoons, which means one coast is always in season and the other is not. This is the only tour here that uses the east as well as the south, so it can run at any time of year - and it gives you the ancient cities, the hill country and two coasts in fifteen days.

It starts quietly at Negombo, then goes north to Anuradhapura and Mihintale, with an afternoon at the Hurulu eco park for elephants. Trincomalee is next: Fort Frederick and the Koneswaram temple on Swami Rock, a swim at Marble Beach, a day at Pigeon Island for reef and blacktip reef sharks, and a whale and dolphin cruise if the season is right. Then back inland for Polonnaruwa, Sigiriya and a Minneriya safari, Dambulla's caves and a cycle through a village for lunch. Kandy, the botanical gardens and Ambuluwawa's spiral tower follow, then the tea road: Pedro Estate, Gregory Lake, Hakgala's gardens, and Horton Plains at dawn for World's End and Baker's Falls. The scenic rail descent to Ella, the Nine Arch Bridge and Little Adam's Peak lead to a full day in Yala and a last afternoon in Galle.

Practically: the east coast suits May to September and the south November to April, and we run the loop in whichever direction keeps you in the dry one. The hotels are five-star, the drives are spaced, and fifteen days is enough that the two long legs do not dominate the trip.

North To South Expedition.summary: From the northern tip to the southern coast: Jaffna's kovils and islands, Mannar's flamingos and ancient baobab, the sacred cities, then the beaches.
North To South Expedition.story:
The north is the part of Sri Lanka most itineraries never reach, and it is a different country in feel: Tamil-speaking, flat and hot, full of Hindu kovils and a history that runs alongside the Sinhalese story rather than behind it. This trip begins there and travels the length of the island to finish on the south coast.

A short flight or a long drive takes you to Jaffna. Nallur Kandaswamy kovil at evening aarti, the old fort and the Dutch museum, the public library rebuilt after the war, Casuarina Beach, and a boat out to Nainativu for the Nagapooshani Amman temple and its Buddhist stupa. Delft Island, reached by ferry, has wild ponies descended from Dutch horses and a coral fort; Point Pedro is the northernmost tip, which you can stand on. Then west to Mannar for Adam's Bridge, a baobab tree older than a thousand years, and a bird sanctuary that fills with flamingos and migrants. Anuradhapura and a Wilpattu mini-safari follow, then Polonnaruwa, Sigiriya, Dambulla and the Minneriya gathering, Kandy, the tea country, Horton Plains, Ella, Udawalawe and a full day in Yala. The last two days are the coast: whales off Mirissa and the ramparts of Galle.

Pack for heat and dust in the north and cold nights in the hills; shoulders and knees covered for the temples. The flight to Jaffna saves a full day, and the hotels are luxury grade, including a Jaffna heritage hotel and a tented camp in Yala.

Luxury Grand Tour.summary: Eighteen unhurried days: every ancient city, both coasts, the hill country and three national parks, with a private guide throughout.
Luxury Grand Tour.story:
Eighteen days is long enough to stop thinking about the next transfer. This is the full island with a private guide and vehicle from the first airport pickup to the last, both coasts, all three ancient capitals, the hill country at its own pace, and three national parks rather than one.

Colombo gets two proper days - the National Museum, Viharamahadevi Park, Mount Lavinia at sunset, an Ayurvedic treatment that takes an afternoon - before the run north to Negombo's lagoon and Anuradhapura, where Mihintale at dawn is worth the early start. Wilpattu for a game drive, then Trincomalee: Koneswaram on its rock, the Kanniya hot springs, a private snorkelling charter at Pigeon Island and a whale and dolphin cruise. Polonnaruwa by boat and bicycle, Sigiriya with a private climb and a hot-air balloon over the Cultural Triangle if the weather agrees. Kandy, Peradeniya's gardens and an Ayurvedic consultation; then the tea country - Pedro Estate, a sommelier session, Horton Plains at first light and the Moon Plains in the afternoon. Ella and the Nine Arch Bridge, Udawalawe's elephants and the transit home, and a full day in Yala, which holds the highest leopard density anywhere. The trip finishes with whales off Mirissa and a last walk around Galle Fort.

No more than two nights in any one place after the first week, and every stop has been chosen for the hotel as much as the location. Ultra-luxury throughout, from a city hotel in Colombo to a tented camp in Yala.

Ultimate Ceylon Odyssey.summary: The whole island, north and east included: Jaffna and Delft, the ancient cities, Arugam Bay's surf, the tea country, then Yala and the south coast.
Ultimate Ceylon Odyssey.story:
Twenty days, fifteen locations, both coasts and every region of the island - for travellers who suspect they will only do this once and would rather not leave a corner out. The north and the east are the difference: Jaffna's peninsula, Delft's wild ponies, and the surf coast at Arugam Bay, which almost no itinerary of this length includes.

Colombo eases you in, with the National Museum, the Pettah and an Ayurvedic treatment, then Negombo's fishing harbour at dawn and a kayak through the Dutch canal. A one-hour flight reaches Jaffna: the Nallur kovil at evening ceremony, the fort, a boat to Nainativu, and a day on Delft Island among the ponies and the coral walls. Anuradhapura and a Wilpattu game drive, then Trincomalee - Koneswaram, the Kanniya springs, and Pigeon Island's reef and reef sharks - before the east coast drive to Arugam Bay, where the point break is the reason surfers come and Kumana National Park is a morning away. Polonnaruwa, Sigiriya, Kaudulla's elephant gathering and the Dambulla caves follow, then Kandy, the blue train into the hills, Heritance Tea Factory, Pedro Estate's high tea and Horton Plains with its 880-metre cliff. Ella, Udawalawe's elephants, Yala's dawn leopard drive, whales off Mirissa and a farewell dinner inside Galle Fort.

The east coast is at its best from May to September and the south from November to April, so we set the direction of travel around your dates. Twenty days is the only way to include the north and the east without a single rushed morning, and the hotels are the best on the island at every stop.
